title: Cross-implementation study manifest
description: One record per cross-implementation study: one claim, one candidate revision, one pinned reference implementation, and the datasets and parameter sets the comparison actually covered. REFERENCE_SLOTS in src/validation/crossCheck.ts holds one reference per claim, which cannot express several datasets or parameter sets per claim; these manifests are the canonical record and the slots stay as the compact runtime summary. Validated by scripts/verify-cross-implementation-study.mjs, which implements the subset of JSON Schema used here without a runtime dependency and adds the cross-checks a schema cannot express. Writing a manifest does not move any claim's evidence level; promotion is a separate, human act recorded in docs/validation/claim-register.yaml.

studyId.description: Stable identity. An example manifest must be prefixed EXAMPLE- and carry example: true, so a reader and the verifier agree about what is real.

claimId.description: Must exist in docs/validation/claim-register.yaml. The verifier reads that register and never writes it.

example.description: True only for a template manifest. An example is excluded from every summary count whatever its status, and may not carry a result.

protocolDigest.description: sha256 over the canonical protocol object (claimId, dataset ids, parameter sets, metrics) as registered BEFORE the study ran. The verifier recomputes it, so a tolerance loosened after seeing the result no longer matches. See the WHY note in the verifier for what this does and does not prove.

protocolRef.description: The frozen protocol this study runs under, in validation/protocols/. Required by rule R12 for any non-example manifest whose status asserts a measured outcome: protocolDigest alone is recomputed from the manifest, so it cannot witness a record rewritten whole, and a protocol record written before the study can. The verifier checks that the protocol exists, that its digest still matches, that it governs this claim, and that this manifest's metrics, datasets and parameter sets are the ones it admits.

status.description: See STUDY_STATUSES in scripts/verify-cross-implementation-study.mjs for what each value means and why blocked-external is separate from unavailable.

statusReason.description: Why the status is what it is, in one sentence. Required for every status, including agree.

result.description: Present only when the study produced numbers. A status of pending or not-executed with a result block is rejected: a count can only come from a study that ran.

rawArtifacts.description: The primary records: candidate output, reference output, the command, the environment capture. Each path is repo-relative and each sha256 is recomputed from the file on disk.

derivedArtifacts.description: Anything computed FROM the raw artifacts. Each one names the raw artifacts it came from and carries the digest of that input set, so a derived summary that no longer follows from the raw records is rejected.

freeze.description: Where the tolerance was frozen, when the default branch cannot show it. A squash merge collapses a preregistration commit and its result into one, so the two-commit sequence scripts/verify-freeze-claims.mjs reads is gone. Naming the commit keeps the claim checkable; it is weaker than reachable history and that check says so.

witnessCommit.description: Full SHA of the commit that carried this record at an unmeasured status.

witness.description: What that commit was and why the history cannot show it.

protocolId.description: The protocolId of a record in validation/protocols/, which is also its filename before .protocol.json.

digest.description: The protocol record's own digest, as this study read it. Recomputed by the verifier from the record on disk, so a protocol edited after a study cited it stops matching.

candidate.description: The OpenLiDARViewer side of the comparison.

reference.description: The independent implementation. A container digest is the ideal pin; when there is none, the executable path, the reported version and the exact command line are all required, and containerPinning must say not-executed.

datasetId.description: A registered identifier, not prose. The shape rule lives in the verifier (DATASET_ID_PATTERN) rather than here, so a free-text dataset id is rejected by the named R2 rule with an explanation instead of a generic pattern failure; membership is checked against validation/datasets/dataset-register.yaml once that register exists.

metrics.description: The agreement gate, registered before the study ran and covered by protocolDigest.

derivedFrom.description: Paths of the rawArtifacts entries this was computed from. Every path must be one of them.

inputsDigest.description: sha256 over the canonical {path, sha256} list of derivedFrom, recomputed by the verifier from the files on disk.

scope.description: What this study supports and what it does not. A supported entry names one dataset and one parameter set that the study actually listed; nothing broader may be approved.
